cfdTrading.question: What is CFD trading?
cfdTrading.answer: CFD trading allows you to trade on the price movement of selected financial instruments without owning the underlying asset.

markets.question: Which markets can I trade with GTCFX?
markets.answer: Depending on your account type and region, you may access Forex, Metals, Energy, Indices, Commodities, Shares, Crypto CFDs and Futures CFDs.

leverage.question: What is leverage in trading?
leverage.answer: Leverage allows you to control a larger trading position with a smaller amount of capital. It can increase both potential gains and potential losses.

spreadsAndCommissions.question: How do spreads and commissions work?
spreadsAndCommissions.answer: The spread is the difference between the bid and ask price. Some account types may also apply a commission per trade or per lot.

margin.question: What is margin and how is it calculated?
margin.answer: Margin is the amount required to open and maintain a trading position. It depends on the instrument, position size, leverage and market conditions.

questions.question: How do I open a live trading account with GTCFX?
questions.answer: Click “Open Account” at the top of any page, complete the online registration form (3-5 minutes), upload your proof of identity (passport/ID) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement). Verification typically completes within 1 business day, after which you can fund your account and start trading.

questions.question: What documents are required for KYC verification?
questions.answer: You usually need a valid government-issued photo ID plus a recent proof of address such as a utility bill or bank statement that matches your registration details.

questions.question: How long does account approval usually take?
questions.answer: Most applications are reviewed within one business day, though complex cases or incomplete documents can take a little longer.

questions.question: Can I open a corporate or joint account?
questions.answer: Yes. Business and joint account applications are available, but they require additional documentation for ownership, authorization, and verification.

questions.question: What account types and base currencies are available?
questions.answer: Available account types and supported base currencies can vary by entity and region. The registration flow and support team can confirm the latest options for your jurisdiction.

questions.question: Is there a minimum deposit to open an account?
questions.answer: Minimum deposits depend on the account type and payment method. You will see the available funding requirements during onboarding or in your client portal.

questions.question: How do I switch between Standard, Pro and ECN accounts?
questions.answer: You can request an additional account type from your client portal or through support, subject to eligibility and entity-specific availability.

questions.question: Which payment methods are available for deposits?
questions.answer: GTCFX supports a range of local and international funding methods depending on your region, including bank transfer, cards, and selected e-wallet options.

questions.question: How long do withdrawals take to process?
questions.answer: Withdrawal review times vary by method and compliance checks, but requests are generally processed promptly during business hours.

questions.question: Are there any deposit or withdrawal fees?
questions.answer: Platform fees may depend on the method used and the receiving institution. Your client portal will show the latest available options.

questions.question: How do I download MT4 or MT5?
questions.answer: Download links for desktop and mobile platforms are available from the platform pages and inside your client area after registration.

questions.question: Can I use MT4/MT5 on Mac and mobile?
questions.answer: Yes. Both platforms are available across desktop and mobile environments, with setup steps depending on your device.

questions.question: What should I do if the platform will not connect?
questions.answer: Double-check your login, server, and password details first. If the issue continues, reinstall the platform or contact support for the correct server and account credentials.

questions.question: Why was my order rejected or requoted?
questions.answer: Order execution can be affected by market volatility, pricing changes, margin availability, or instrument trading hours.

questions.question: How are swaps and commissions calculated?
questions.answer: Charges depend on the instrument, account type, and holding period. Platform specifications and contract details provide the latest values.

questions.question: Can I place pending orders and set stop-loss levels?
questions.answer: Yes. MT4 and MT5 support market, pending, stop-loss, and take-profit instructions, subject to product and execution rules.

questions.question: How can I keep my account secure?
questions.answer: Use a strong password, protect your device, enable any available security steps, and never share your credentials with third parties.

questions.question: What if I notice suspicious activity?
questions.answer: Change your password immediately and contact support so the team can review recent account activity and help secure access.

questions.question: Can I reset my password online?
questions.answer: Yes. Password recovery is typically available through the login flow or client portal, subject to identity confirmation.

items.q: What's the difference between MT4 and MT5?
items.a: MT5 offers more built-in technical indicators and timeframes, a more advanced strategy tester with multi-threaded backtesting, an integrated economic calendar, and support for hedging and netting account modes. MT4 remains popular for its simplicity, lighter resource use, and the largest existing library of community EAs and indicators. Neither platform is strictly better — the right choice depends on whether you prioritize MT4's simplicity and EA ecosystem or MT5's broader toolset and multi-asset support.

items.q: Can I run Expert Advisors on MT5?
items.a: Yes. MT5 supports Expert Advisors written in MQL5, which is not directly compatible with MQL4 code — EAs and custom indicators built for MT4 generally need to be rewritten or converted to work on MT5.

Yes. MT5 supports both netting and hedging account types. With hedging mode enabled, you can hold simultaneous long and short positions on the same instrument — useful for advanced strategies like grid trading, lock-and-hedge, and multi-timeframe position management. Contact support@gtcfx.com to confirm which mode is available on your account type.

items.question: Is swap charged every day?
items.answer: Yes. Swap is charged daily for every overnight position. If you close before the market rollover (usually 5 PM New York time), no swap is applied for that day.

items.question: Which day is the triple swap day?
items.answer: Wednesday. Since forex settlement is T+2, holding a position overnight on Wednesday accounts for the weekend, when markets are closed — so swap is charged at three times the standard daily rate to cover Saturday and Sunday.

items.question: Can swap rates change?

Rates shown in our overnight fee table reflect the current day and can move as market conditions change.

items.question: What is an Economic Calendar?
items.answer: An economic calendar is a schedule of upcoming economic events and data releases — such as interest rate decisions, GDP figures, employment reports, and inflation data — that can move financial markets. Traders use it to plan positions ahead of high-impact events.

items.question: How do I use the Economic Calendar to trade?
items.answer: Filter events by date range, impact level (High / Medium / Low), and country. Before a high-impact release, check the forecast vs. prior values. If the actual beats the forecast, the affected currency or instrument typically strengthens — and vice versa. Always use proper risk management around news events.

items.question: What does the impact level (High / Medium / Low) mean?
items.answer: Impact level indicates how much a data release has historically moved the markets. High-impact events — like Non-Farm Payrolls, FOMC decisions, or CPI — tend to cause significant price swings. Medium-impact events cause moderate moves, while Low-impact events rarely shift prices materially.

items.question: What time zone does the calendar use?
items.answer: By default, the calendar displays event times in your local time zone. You can switch to UTC or any other time zone using the timezone selector at the top of the calendar.

items.question: Is the Economic Calendar data real-time?
items.answer: Yes. Actual release values are updated in real-time as official data is published. Forecast and prior figures are sourced from leading financial data providers and updated regularly.

infoCards.whatIsDescription: The Financial Commission was established to be a neutral third-party committee to fairly review and resolve complaints. process.title: How are the funds managed?
process.description: The Compensation Fund is a compensation mechanism maintained by the Financial Commission for eligible clients of its members. According to the Financial Commission’s Rules, the Fund is held in a separate bank account and may be used to satisfy an eligible Award if a member fails or refuses to comply with that Award, or ceases to be a member before paying it. Any payment is subject to the applicable Rules, compensation limits and available fund balance. The Fund is not an insurance policy, deposit-guarantee scheme or general protection against trading losses or broker insolvency. It applies only to eligible claims made against the specific legal entity that holds Financial Commission membership.
